Sleep stage reflect_profile: through the per-session runner (each consolidated session once, done marker per session and member fingerprint), call the reflect role with the dated turn lines; the structured reply is a list of insights with evidence indices (prompt reflect.yaml, token budget 384).

Each insight with valid evidence is deposited through the governed reflect door as a reflective record (role assistant, channel reflection, message_id 'reflected:<session key>', parents = evidence turns).

Read side: read.profile_header_packing replaces the plain profile header by a packed block: three gated searches (semantic consolidation summaries, reflective insights, other hits) packed in that order within read.profile_header_budget (300 tokens, capped at PROFILE_PACK_MAX_SHARE of the budget); skipped for temporal questions and general-knowledge questions when the profile gates are on.

algorithms: session boundary detection by time gap
LLM insight extraction with evidence indices
priority packing summaries then insights then hits under a token budget

steps.what: Existing extract_graph facts are indexed first: every live or closed fact of the namespace goes into an EdgeKeyIndex by v2 key, by base (from its edge_base: tag) or as a v1 alias key.

For each extracted edge compute the v1 key (namespace, src, rel, dst; with isolation.scope_keys_v2 the tenant+owner identity) and the v2 base key = hash(scope, kind, src, rel, dst, extras) where extras are the event day and numerals for dated event edges.
Occurrence = hash of the sorted cited turns (content fingerprint @ valid_from), so re-extracting the same turns gives the same key (replay idempotent) while a new statement later gives a new one.

EdgeKeyIndex.decide: duplicate if the exact v2 key exists; duplicate via base if a live sibling of the same base exists; duplicate via alias if a live v1 key exists; new_occurrence if only closed siblings exist (the A -> B -> A return); else new.
A 'duplicate' only adds edge_source provenance to the existing fact (no write). A stale duplicate (record closed since) is re-checked against storage and turned into new_occurrence.
A new key is written as the fact's message_id and the base is stored as an edge_base: tag so later occurrences find their siblings. A derive.graph.key tap event records outcome, via and kind.

libraries: store/keys.py (F-01 pure key functions, shared with LIB-35 edge compiler)

storage: Writes an extra edge_base:<hash> tag on each extract_graph fact; message_id carries the v2 key. Reads all prior extract_graph facts at sweep start.
cost: No model calls; a full graph rebuild is needed because keys change, so the row re-ingests (150 min row, about 2.5 h).
inputs: extract_graph facts (this is the gc3 base).
outputs: Fewer or different duplicates: an edge restated after a different value is kept as a new occurrence instead of being absorbed by the closed one. Stored records change identity; QA effect is expected near zero (NONINF).
failure_modes: Only visible on questions with value reversals; most LoCoMo questions are unaffected.
Changes record ids and keys, so it cannot be compared record-for-record with S02.

  D -->|new or new occurrence| F[write fact with edge_base tag]

steps.what: Insert the stage in the order after reflect_profile.
Per namespace under the write lock: read live semantic records; keep keyed facts tagged kind:state from non-derived channels (is_input_fact) and project them to assertion envelopes.
Build value histories per (subject, attribute) from the envelopes (LIB-02 replay, event-time ordered).
Invalidate by changed group: for each stored answer recompute its probe fingerprint; if different, mark the group stale, refresh the answer; retire duplicates and emptied answers.

Add new answers for groups that have a current or open-contest value, newest group first, up to offline.standing_max_answers (50); evict idle (only once reads were logged), low-hit-rate or surplus answers.

Write each answer as a derived semantic record (channel standing, text render_answer, tags carry question key, dependency fingerprint, seq, contested flag; parents = supporting facts; trust capped at the weakest parent) through the derived write door; archive retired ones.

Read side (read.standing_v2): pick the topic entities of the best keyed semantic hits, take their top attribute as the question key, select fresh answers within read.standing_answers_budget (stale ones, whose live fact set differs, are never shown and are logged as misses) and prepend one lead block 'standing answers' plus guarded standing instructions.

find_observations runs the five miners: recurrence (regular weekly/monthly/yearly intervals), frequency (N occurrences in a trailing window), trend (numeric attribute over 3+ dated points), co-occurrence (two kinds in the same session/day), preference stability (restated across sessions).
Same-day same-kind assertions count once (independence); a preference restated by one source family has capped confidence.
Invalidate: stored observations whose supporting facts are no longer live, or that the new run no longer produces, are archived (observation->retired).

steps.what: Insert compile_edges before summarize_entities.
Per namespace under the lock, read live semantic records and keep eligible assertions (facts, not summaries or cues).

EdgeCompiler: convert each fact to an assertion envelope (store.envelope.to_envelope with the tri-temporal fields), enrich from the rel:/dst:/kind: tags, resolve subject and object to existing ent:<ns>:<canonical> nodes (entity policy applied), scope by tenant+owner if isolation.scope_keys_v2.

compile_edges (LIB-35) emits an assertion node, role edges and one binary projection edge per fact with A-B-A occurrence keys, valid_from/valid_to (closed when superseded), evidence ids, trust; tentative rule tags hypothetical, planned, reported, question, unconfirmed assistant or partly bound edges.
LinkProjection writes the delta as LINK events (idempotent: only edges whose stored form differs), with typed props in payload and the marker 'compiled=edge_compiler_v2'.
Retire: records that are no longer assertions (erased, hidden, archived without successor) get tombstone LINKs and their unused assertion/value/time nodes are deleted.

trigger: Sleep stages decay_sweep (tiers) and compress (multi-resolution plan), stage order position unchanged (after reorganize, check_watches, session_lifecycle).

steps.what: decay_sweep delegates to decay_sweep_v2.

Per record (episodic, semantic, resource; not deleted/quarantined/legal-hold) compute activation = w_rec * exp(-idle_days/S_kind) + w_freq * min(1, ln(1+n)/ln(1+n_sat)) + w_imp * importance, with idle_days counted from the later of last_accessed_at and recorded_at.

Tier plan with hysteresis: move down while activation is below a boundary, move up only past boundary plus 0.05; protected records (pinned, standing, contested, protected kinds) are never moved colder and a cold one is restored to hot.
Each move is a DECAY_TRANSITION delta on the tier (reason idle, reactivated or protected_restore). Nothing is deleted and tiers do not change ranking (O-22).
compress runs the zstd step as before, then multires_v2 plans paragraph/sentence/keyword jobs for cold or dormant groups; with decay_multires_jobs 0 it only plans and reports (no summarize calls).

outputs: No change to answers (PARITY rule). Deferred in the queue: ranking-neutral by design.
failure_modes: Cannot show an effect in a single-build eval because nothing ages; real value needs long-running stores.

steps.what: After placement and ordering of the volatile records, if read.trust_rendering is on call trust_render(volatile).
Each record becomes a TrustItem with an envelope (source trust, src_class, status), its quarantined flag and instruction_flag.
classify assigns a band by precedence quarantined > contested > tentative > low_trust > trusted (low-trust = source trust below TRUST_DEFAULT 0.5 or src_class tool/document/external).

render() orders bands trusted, contested, tentative, low-trust; low-trust text is NFKC-normalised, control and zero-width chars stripped, brackets and backticks replaced, imperative phrases wrapped in double angle brackets and the line flagged instruction-like, then emitted as a quoted escaped string; contested values of one key share a line; quarantined records are withheld.
Each output line becomes a copy of its first source record with the line text as content; the old B6 untrusted-note wrapper is disabled while the flag is on.
Tap compose.render.bands logs band counts, neutralised and injection-like counts.

settings.profile trust-v2 on scr-gc3-graph-jina: isolation.scope_keys_v2, viewer_required, owner_bound_handles; privacy.erasure_v2, erasure_redact_hidden; retention.v2; audit.chain_v2; consent.v2; firewall.gates_v2; integrity.enabled, horizon_v2

trigger: Mostly per write and per read, with sleep-side effects in how derived stages read and write. Few of these flags add a sleep stage.

steps.what: isolation.scope_keys_v2: extract_graph and the edge compiler key edges by typed tenant+owner identity instead of the namespace string (session never part of a key); the read cache key uses the same scope.

isolation.viewer_required + owner_bound_handles: a read must carry a viewer bound to the principal; derived records inherit the intersection of their parents' visibility/participant tags (restrict_to_parents). This may refuse the eval adapter's unscoped reads (SCREENS.md: RUN_FAILED is then the finding).

firewall.gates_v2 (needs firewall.enabled): gate 1 on insert, gate 2 filters extraction inputs in the session stages, gate 3 on derived writes (derive_hold): a flagged derived record is written but held in quarantine, never served or used as a parent.

consent.v2 and privacy.erasure_v2 turn on the live_gate for every sleep stage: offline_live drops erased/hidden ids, consent-refused records, quarantined records and subjects marked do-not-derive before a stage reads them; write_derived refuses (holds) derived records the consent registry denies.

privacy.erasure_v2: forgetting hides dependants and queues them (LIB-09 plan); erasure_redact_hidden hard-forgets hidden rows. The erasure_rederive sleep stage that re-derives them is only scheduled when privacy.erasure_rederive is ALSO on, which the preset does not set.

retention.v2 + audit.chain_v2 + integrity.horizon_v2: retention classes plan expiry (retention_expire is scheduled only when retention.classes is non-empty; none is set), event_log_prune stamps rebuild limited only in rolling mode, the audit log is hash-chained (verify_audit_chain_v2) and the trust horizon bounds cross-agent reach via grant attenuation (LIB-21).

Sleep-side: retention_expire and erasure_rederive are not scheduled by the preset, so those parts are off despite retention.v2/erasure_v2.
Gates can hold benign derived facts (false positives; MINJA false positives target at most 1%).

trigger: Per write window, per sleep stage, per read: runtime plumbing around existing work.

steps.what: workers.outbox: window jobs become durable outbox rows drained by an inline runner (matters only if windows are on; gc3 has no write.window_extract, so this is idle).

runtime.scheduler_v2: micro-batched encoder executors for document and query embedding, backpressure policy and SLO ledger. Its background-priority sleep class only applies to sleep_v2 jobs (off here).

economy.ledger_v2: every sleep stage runs inside a cost scope (namespace '-' pool, layer = stage), counting model calls, tokens, latency and embed calls; cost_report() reads it. ledger_persist keeps compact rows in <path>.cost so totals survive restarts.

read.cache.enabled: whole read results cached by scope, viewer, query, config, model ids and store/erasure generations; every hit is revalidated (POL-1) against the live store; reads naming a session_id are never cached. In QA each question is asked once, so hits are rare.
read.parallel_legs: independent retrieval legs run with asyncio.gather; the result order stays the sequential order.

settings.arm: scr-gc3-graph-jina (reference of every B3/B5/B8 GC row; run id v2-S02-i2)

trigger: Once per conversation, after all sessions are written: the eval adapter calls Memory.sleep() in build() (memspine_system.py:build), which runs run_sleep_cycle over sleep_stage_order(ctx). No offline.* flag is set, so the order is the plain SLEEP_CYCLE_ORDER with no extra stages and the blocking path (not sleep_v2).

steps.what: Order. SLEEP_CYCLE_ORDER = consolidate, mine_facts, anticipate, reflect_profile, extract_graph, summarize_entities, reorganize, check_watches, session_lifecycle, decay_sweep, compress, sleep_compute, event_log_prune. sleep_stage_order() only inserts extra stages when their flag is on (predict_calibrate, project_facts, rule_edges, pattern_observations, standing_answers, reconcile, histories, compile_edges, erasure_rederive, retention_expire); none is on in gc3, so all 13 names run in this order, each timed and costed through run_sleep_stage.

1 consolidate (RUNS, no LLM): detect sessions by a 30-minute gap over live episodic records; for each closed session of at least 3 records write ONE semantic summary record (channel consolidation, parents = the session turns, trust = min of members). No summarize role is bound in gc3, so the text is the deterministic extractive fallback (max 600 chars). It also emits the CONSOLIDATE/session index that extract_graph reads.

2 mine_facts (SKIPPED): consolidation.mine_facts is off and no extract role is bound. 3 anticipate (SKIPPED): consolidation.anticipate off. 4 reflect_profile (SKIPPED): consolidation.reflect_profile off and no reflect role (this is the stage S01/gc9 turns on).

5 extract_graph (RUNS, LLM role extract_edges): granularity=session. Group the live episodic turns of each consolidated session (skipping cues, entity-summary and window-episode records, quarantined or instruction-flagged turns); skip a session whose membership fingerprint already has a stage_done marker. For each remaining session, render a numbered transcript '[n] [date] turn', optionally ask the GLiNER2 decision provider for allowed entity names (only if configured; not in gc3), then ONE structured call (prompt extract_edges@session, 1 round) returns edges {src_entity, rel, dst_entity, fact, kind state|event, valid_from/valid_to, confidence, episode_indices}. Turns not in any consolidated session (sessions under 3 records) fall back to one per-record call with the plain extract_edges prompt.

5b Entity resolution (resolve=rules, no LLM): every src/dst name goes through the ladder exact canonical match -> alias table (MARKER events) -> top-15 embedding candidates (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B) -> entropy gate -> MinHash character-shingle Jaccard >= 0.9, with a trust guard; merges are logged as one entity_resolved MARKER.

5c Write: each edge becomes a semantic fact (content = edge.fact, entity = src, attribute = rel for kind:state, no attribute for kind:event; tags kind:/rel:/dst:; channel extract_graph; parents = the cited turns), written through the semantic door (firewall trust cap, M5 dedup, M4 ladder so a newer state value supersedes). A verbatim duplicate only adds edge_source provenance. Then an asserted LINK from every parent turn to the fact (weight = min of confidence and trusts, subject to the link budget) and a graph_extracted MARKER watermark per source and a per-session stage_done marker.

6 summarize_entities (RUNS, LLM role summarize_entity, only when needed): the graph projector has turned entity/dst names of live records into ent:<ns>:<name> nodes with mentions links (associative.entity_nodes). For each entity node whose member fingerprint changed, build dated fact lines; if the joined lines fit 2000 chars the summary is those lines (free, no call); otherwise entities are batched (30 per call) into prompt summarize_entity.yaml, with a newest-lines fallback on failure. Each result is a derived semantic record (channel entity_summary, tag about:<Name>, parents = the members, trust = min), firewall-screened, and an entity_summarized MARKER stores the watermark.

7 reorganize (SKIPPED in practice): needs a graph store and either the [community] extra (graspologic-native, absent from the dev venv) or community.algorithm=lpa; with the default algorithm auto and no extra it returns skipped. If it did run it would write community summary parents.

8 check_watches, 9 session_lifecycle, 10 decay_sweep, 11 compress, 12 sleep_compute, 13 event_log_prune: check_watches only logs fired prospective watches (none); session_lifecycle needs sessions.passive_after (unset: skipped); decay_sweep moves idle records between tiers by days since recorded_at/last access (all records are fresh in an eval, so no moves); compress zstd-compresses cold-tier content (none cold); sleep_compute is the no-op E7 hook; event_log_prune runs only in rolling event-log mode (skipped).

algorithms: LLM edge extraction with episode_indices citations
entity resolution ladder: exact, alias table, embedding top-15, MinHash Jaccard 0.9 with entropy gate and trust guard
M4 supersede ladder for state facts
libraries: LIB-02 integrate ladder (via the semantic write door)
external: sentence-transformers Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (resolution candidates, entity embeddings)
external: sqlite event log, lancedb, tantivy (indexes updated by projectors as the stages append events)

models.calls: 1 per consolidated session (not yet fingerprinted) + 1 per loose turn outside any session; about 550-650 calls for the 272-session full set per GAP_REGISTER L; a 3-conversation sample is proportionally smaller
models.prompt: src/memspine/prompts/defaults/extract_edges@session.yaml (session) and extract_edges.yaml (loose turns); the layout-v2 copies under defaults/v2 are used only with prompts.layout_v2 (off)

Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (cuda, bf16)

storage: Reads the event log and the episodic/semantic stores. Appends WRITE events (consolidation summaries, extract_graph facts, entity_summary records), LINK events (asserted, mentions, derived_from), MARKER events (graph_extracted, entity_resolved, entity_summarized, stage_done per session) and DECAY_TRANSITION events (supersede/archive). Projectors update the vector, FTS and graph stores.
cost: Dominated by extract_edges: one 9B call per session at roughly 1.5-2 h for the 10-conversation set (GAP_REGISTER L estimate); the stage list adds no GPU model other than the embedder. Doc: gc3 about 39 min per 3-conversation sample run ('11 gc9 / 24 gc2 / 39 gc3' min engine-LLM ingest in SCREENS.md).
inputs: Episodic turns written with group/session ids and event dates; an extract_edges role; associative memory enabled so the graph projector exists.
outputs: Semantic summaries, graph facts with parents, asserted/mentions links, entity-summary records. The read side then uses read.graph_leg (BFS depth 2, 10 seeds), graph_node_search and read.entity_summaries over these.
failure_modes: A failed extract_edges call leaves no watermark: the session is retried next sweep (errors counted in the stage stats, status partial).
reorganize is a silent skip without graspologic-native: no community summaries in any gc3-based arm unless offline.communities_v2 is on.
Session grouping depends on consolidate having produced a session index; sessions under 3 records are extracted per record.
Sleep has no budget cap in this arm (offline.budget_v2 off): a slow Ollama server stalls the build.
